content:
Scientific Concept: Lambda-CDM Standard Cosmological Model
Domain: space / cosmology
Definition: Standard cosmological model of the Universe based on General Relativity, expanding space according to Friedmann-Lemaitre-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) metric.

Principles:
Hubble-Lemaitre Law: Recessional velocity of distant galaxies is proportional to distance: v = H_0 * d
Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB): Thermal blackbody radiation remnant from recombination era (T_0 = 2.7255 K).
Energy Budget: ~68.3% Dark Energy (Cosmological constant Lambda), ~26.8% Cold Dark Matter (CDM), ~4.9% Ordinary Baryonic Matter.
Gravitational Collapse & Compact Objects: Black holes (Schwarzschild radius r_s = 2GM/c^2), Neutron stars (TOV limit ~2.2 M_sun).

Experimental Proofs:
Edwin Hubble 1929 distance-redshift measurements using Cepheid variable stars
Penzias & Wilson 1964 discovery of CMB isotropic radiation; COBE, WMAP, Planck precision measurements
Type Ia Supernovae 1998 discovery of accelerating cosmic expansion (Perlmutter, Riess, Schmidt)
Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) direct shadow imaging of supermassive black holes M87* and Sgr A*

Applications:
Space exploration mission planning
Interplanetary navigation
Deep space telemetry
